answer: Trust propagates through degree-normalized, bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, so voting influence depends on reachable, independently supported attestations rather than raw identities. For a sybil set S, conductance φ(S)=cut(S,¬S)/min(vol(S),vol(¬S)) measures its external connectivity; when this cut is sparse, few walk transitions carry trust out of S, limiting aggregate weight under capped propagation. A prism of paths cannot erase this bottleneck: glacier-like persistence or ivory-bright labels add no edges.
